evidence.text: miR-9* (the passenger strand of miR-9, also denoted miR-9-3p) directly targets the 3'UTR of BAF53a (ACTL6A), repressing its translation. BAF53a is a subunit of the neural-progenitor BAF (npBAF) chromatin remodelling complex. Its downregulation by miR-9* and miR-124 is required for the switch from npBAF to neuronal nBAF (containing BAF53b/ACTL6B) during post-mitotic neuronal differentiation.

miR-124 cooperates with miR-9* to repress BAF53a (ACTL6A) via its 3'UTR. Both miRNAs must act together for full repression; their combined activity triggers the BAF53a-to-BAF53b subunit switch that is essential for dendritic morphogenesis in post-mitotic neurons.

miR-124 represses PTBP1 (polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1), a splicing repressor that maintains non-neuronal splicing patterns. Downregulation of PTBP1 by miR-124 during neuronal differentiation derepresses neuron-specific alternative exons and permits upregulation of the neuronal paralog PTBP2/nPTB.

miR-9 directly targets REST (RE1-silencing transcription factor / NRSF), a master transcriptional repressor of neuronal genes in non-neuronal cells. miR-9-mediated downregulation of REST derepresses a large battery of neuron-specific genes. REST and miR-9 form a double-negative feedback loop, as REST itself represses the miR-9 locus in progenitors.

miR-9 targets CoREST (RCOR1), a corepressor that partners with REST and LSD1 to silence neuronal gene promoters. Downregulation of RCOR1 by miR-9 dismantles the REST/CoREST/LSD1 repressor complex, complementing the direct targeting of REST itself.

miR-124 (and miR-9) target Rap2a, a small GTPase that promotes dendritic pruning. Repression of RAP2A by these brain-enriched miRNAs permits dendritic elaboration during neuronal maturation. RAP2A repression is part of the broader miR-9/miR-124 programme that drives irreversible neuronal commitment.
